title: The Mineral Detective Solving Big Problems With Rocks
summary:
Aaron Celestian works with minerals at the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County. He is the curator of mineral sciences. He studies minerals and how they work with living things. He tries to work out how Earth changed millions of years ago. He is also working on cures for diseases made with minerals.

To answer his questions, Celestian uses X-rays, lasers, nuclear reactors, radio waves, and magnets. If a tool he needs does not exist yet, he builds it himself. He is good with his hands and learns new tools very quickly.

One of his proudest moments came from a long project. His team made a new mineral that cleans water. The work took about 10 years. When a test showed it could clean toxic lead out of water, he called it 'extremely satisfying.' He loves hearing visitors gasp at the crystals in the Gem and Mineral Hall.

Most people think his job is just putting rocks on display. But he says minerals can help fight climate change, cure diseases, clean up the environment, and solve energy problems.
why_it_matters: Rocks are not just for looking at — the minerals inside them could help clean water and protect the planet you will grow up on.

keywords.explanation: Minerals are natural materials found in rocks, like crystals and metals.
A curator is a person who looks after a museum's collection and studies it.
X-rays are a kind of light that can see through things and show what is inside them.
Toxic means poisonous or harmful to people and living things.
Climate change is a long-term change in Earth's weather and temperatures.
